subject: Private VPC availability allocation for customer-managed edge (HaloQuest)
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:31:12 -0700
Subject: Private VPC availability allocation — need clarification

Connor,

We're in the middle of procurement and legal review. Our cloud/network team flagged a concern: in our Private VPC setup we manage the peering and some edge routing — if we hit degraded latency on our side, HaloQuest needs clarity on how uptime/latency SLOs are apportioned. Your standard SLA references "customer-managed network" carveouts but the language is high-level.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept an explicit allocation where end-to-end availability is apportioned 70/30 (customer/network vs Redwood) for customer-controlled peering, and what evidence you would require to validate incidents that fall on our side?

Also attaching a brief pcap and a short mcap summary from last week's incident for context.

Thanks,
Samir
Network Ops, HaloQuest
Attachment: network-traces-20270612.pcap (pcap)
Attachment: haloquest-mcap-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC availability allocation — need clarification

Samir — thanks for the packet captures and context.

Short answer: Redwood is open to a documented shared-responsibility allocation for customer-managed peering, but we need a clear operational definition and evidentiary requirements before we can accept a numerical split in the contract.

Would the HaloQuest team be able to provide:
- a short runbook that shows how peering is configured and who owns BGP/route changes
- examples of the metrics you rely on (eg. 1s p95 egress RTT per region) and where those are published
- a canonical list of your edge IP blocks and any third-party transit providers used

From our side, Ops will want the ability to validate incidents with packet captures, traceroutes, and our own edge telemetry for the same window. I'll coordinate with Marissa on what exact telemetry we require. Looping in Lauren for legal language guidance.

If acceptable, I'll propose a temporary exception framework (30–60 day trial) and a specific clause we can insert into the Private Addendum.

—Connor
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 07:08:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC availability allocation — need clarification

Connor,

Thanks — attached is our 2-page runbook excerpt, plus the mcap. We publish edge metrics to a private Grafana instance (we can grant read-only access). Our transit mix includes two providers and direct peering with Redwood's listed ASNs; the runbook has IP blocks.

We'll grant an Ops contact for the 30-day trial and can provide BGP change logs when applicable. Happy to sign a narrow exception clause for peering-related attribution.

Attachments: haloquest-runbook-excerpt.pdf (pdf)

—Samir

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:21:03 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private VPC availability allocation — proposed exception trial

Hi Lauren/Marissa — forwarding HaloQuest's runbook and traces. Can you review and confirm:
1) whether the proposed 70/30 split is acceptable as a starting point or if Ops/legal want a different framing (eg. attribution-based carveout rather than fixed percentages)
2) what telemetry/evidence Redwood must retain to adjudicate incidents (time windows, packet formats, SPOF checks)

Marissa — high level: can Redwood derive the necessary ID from our edge telemetry and the customer's pcap within 48 hours? If it requires more than that we'll need to set expectations for evidence windows.

Lauren — if we do a 30-day trial period, what contractual language should we propose so it's reversible and doesn't create an open-ended liability?

Thanks,
Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:57:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private VPC availability allocation — proposed exception trial

Connor — reviewed the runbook and traces.

Ops perspective:
- We can validate attribution using synchronized timestamps, TCP packet signatures, and our edge KV cache logs. 48 hours is tight but feasible; 72 hours is safer for cross-team reconciliation.
- Rather than a strict 70/30 number, I recommend an "attribution-first" rule: incidents are attributed by observable fault domain (customer-network vs Redwood-hosted infra). When attribution is unclear after the evidence window, default to a shared-reduction formula capped at 25% credit back to the customer.
- Required evidence: pcap, traceroute, BGP change logs, and our edge latency histogram for the 5-minute incident window. Keep logs for 90 days for auditability during the trial.

I'll prepare a short ops appendix with the exact telemetry fields and retention requirements.

—Marissa
Director, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-telemetry-evidence-spec.md (md)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Rao <samir@haloquest.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 16:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private VPC availability allocation — proposed exception trial

Connor/Marissa/Samir — legal sign-off on a reversible, time-boxed exception looks feasible.

Suggested contract phrasing (high level):
"For Private VPC deployments where the customer controls peering and edge routing, Redwood and Customer will conduct a 60-day Attribution Trial. During the Trial, incidents will be attributed to the party responsible based on mutually agreed evidentiary requirements. If attribution is inconclusive within the agreed evidence window, parties will apply a capped shared-credit mechanism (maximum customer credit 25%). Trial termination or extension requires 14 days' notice by either party."

Two notes:
- Require the customer to grant read-only access to any private monitoring dashboards cited in evidence, and to deliver BGP change logs on request.
- Limit the exception's liability cap to the standard Private Addendum liability ceiling.

Connor — happy to draft the redline. Samir — please confirm HaloQuest can provide the dashboard access and the 60-day trial is acceptable.

—Lauren
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
